Hi Alice / Ben 1 thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we agreed and next steps so everything is aligned: 

Summary of call:
- PayGrid use case: high-throughput customer support triage + transaction-aware answer generation. Latency target <= 250ms p95 for short responses; acceptable throughput ~200 reqs/s for peak lanes.
- Key quality constraints: intent correctness, factuality on transaction metadata (no hallucination on sensitive fields), and minimal latency regressions when switching models.

Recommended initial models (based on our quick benchmarking):
- Mistral-Instruct-34B (Redwood-verified): best cost/quality tradeoff for retrieval-augmented snippets; estimated parity 93-97% vs PayGrid baseline on intent for our prompt set.
- Llama-2-Chat-70B (quantized 8-bit): stronger on instruction-following for complex policy answers, slightly higher cost; parity often 95%+ on intent but watch hallucination for long-tail finance facts.
- Vicuna-13B (optimized): cheap option for low-complexity triage; expect lower intent parity (~88-92) on the first pass.

Parity & acceptance thresholds (recap from discussion):
- PayGrid baseline acceptance threshold: >=95% on intent classification for the qualification prompt-set, and hallucination rate <2% on transaction-sensitive prompts.
- If open models hit these thresholds on our eval, we can propose a staged rollout with canary traffic.

Links & artifacts I uploaded for your team:
- Prompt set (driver prompts used in today's demo): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/shared/paygrid/prompt-set-v1 (CSV attached)
- Lightweight eval dashboard (initial runs): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/shared/paygrid/eval-dashboard

Next steps (action owners & ETA):
1) PayGrid: share 1 representative sample dataset for masked analyses (Ben/Alice) 1 ETA: EOD 2026-10-06. [Action: PayGrid]
2) Redwood: run parity evals across Mistral-Instruct-34B, Llama-2-Chat-70B (8-bit), and PayGrid baseline replica; produce med/long prompt breakdown 1 ETA: 48 hours after data receipt. [Action: Lauren / Marissa]
3) Tech deep-dive to review regression concerns (hallucination cases) and rollout plan 1 schedule for next week pending eval results. [Action: All]

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.csv (attached).

If that matches your notes, can you confirm Ben/Alice and share the sample dataset? Happy to spin the full eval once we have that.

Thanks for the forward 1 ran the first-pass evals on the sample prompt set you attached (small, 120 prompts across short/long/policy categories). High-level notes: 

Initial runs (attached full report): paygrid_eval_report_v1.pdf
- Mistral-Instruct-34B:
  - Intent parity vs PayGrid baseline (v2.3 stub): ~95% overall.
  - Hallucination rate (transaction-sensitive prompts): ~2.6% 1 slightly above PayGrid's target.
  - Strength: concise instruction following and lower latency (p50 ~95ms on our 4xA100 pool).

- Llama-2-Chat-70B (8-bit quantized):
  - Intent parity: ~96.5% overall.
  - Hallucination rate: ~2.9% on sensitive prompts 1 highest of the group but we saw fewer intent misses.
  - Cost: ~1.6x Mistral for equivalent throughput in our infra.

- PayGrid baseline (v2.3 stub):
  - Intent parity baseline by definition 100% vs itself; hallucination measured ~0.8% on same prompt set.

Observations & recommended mitigation paths:
1) Hallucination delta mostly originates from long-form policy explanations where open models attempt to synthesize missing context. We mitigated some cases with stricter system prompts and retrieval augmentation (RAG) in a follow-up run 1 hallucination rates dropped ~0.7-1.0pp depending on model.
2) For parity gating: recommend two-stage acceptance criteria: 
   - Stage A (pre-canary): intent parity >=95% on the main prompt-set and hallucination <=2.0% on sensitive prompts after RAG/system prompt tuning.
   - Stage B (canary): live canary with 5% traffic, validate SLA & monitor for drift over 72 hours, require automated rollback if hallucination >2.5% or error rate increases >1.0pp.
3) Rollout options: prefer Mistral-Instruct-34B initially due to cost/latency 1 Llama-2-Chat-70B is a close second if PayGrid values absolute intent parity above 96% and is willing to accept higher infra cost.

Attached: paygrid_eval_report_v1.pdf (summary + per-prompt breakdown), and prompt set used (paygrid_prompt_set_v1.csv).

Let me know if you want a deeper per-case analysis (I can generate the top-20 hallucination examples).

1Marissa Cole
Applied ML 1 Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: paygrid_eval_report_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 280KB)]

Great work on the initial runs. A few practical items and recommendations to operationalize the acceptance criteria for PayGrid (deal PG-4782):

1) Evaluation scale & statistical gating:
- For pre-canary acceptance, require N >= 1000 prompts sampled across short/long/policy buckets (proportional to PayGrid traffic mix). For parity assertions (>=95%), 95% CI width should be <= ±1.5pp.

2) Regression testing & alerting:
- Add an automated regression suite that runs nightly on a rolling sample of 5k prompts from production-like data (redacted) and surfaces top hallucination cases.
- Hook the suite into Redwood Optimize so we can send model/quantization recommendations if hallucination spikes.

3) Rollout plan (canary):
- Canary: 5% traffic for 72 hours with automated monitoring for intent parity and hallucination thresholds. If anything exceeds gating (hallucination >2.5% or intent drops >3pp), automated rollback to PayGrid baseline.

4) Short-term mitigations to reduce hallucination delta:
- Strict system prompt with instruction to "If unsure, reply: "I don't know, please verify with transaction data.""
- Use retrieval augmentation for policy/transaction answers (indexed) 1 we saw ~0.7pp hallucination improvement in RAG runs.

If you get the sanitized dataset from PayGrid, I recommend we run the full 1k-sample eval and provide a single-slide parity summary for the customer-facing roadmap review. I can partner on the gating tests and alert config.

1Aditya Rao
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
